data.one_liner: Check if an update is available for your Flutter app on Android and iOS.
data.what_it_does: Provides a single asynchronous function to check update availability for your app based on published versions on Android and iOS. Returns a sealed Availability class indicating whether an update is available, no update is available, or the status is unknown.
use_when: You want support for both iOS and Android update checks
You want the bare minimum information about update availability to build your own custom upgrade screen
avoid_when: You want built-in user interfaces or pre-made alert and card widgets for updates
You are testing Android updates locally without publishing an app bundle to Google Play Internal App Sharing
strengths: Simple API with a single function getUpdateAvailability
Supports both iOS and Android platforms
Exposes sealed class Availability for exhaustive switch-case handling
weaknesses: Does not provide any built-in user interfaces or dialogs
Android implementation requires setting up Internal App Sharing and publishing test app bundles to properly test
data.setup_notes: Add dependency to pubspec.yaml. Android testing requires setting up Google Play Internal App Sharing and app signing.
